message.content: READ-ONLY audit of the caliper repo (do not edit, commit, push or open PRs; write only /tmp/claude-501/audit-semantic.md). Use `git fetch origin` and read from origin/main (`git show origin/main:<path>` or a checkout of it in your own worktree). Context: recurring Entire-reviewer findings in crates/semantic and its boundary with crates/core: (1) ABSENCE TREATED AS EVIDENCE: `settled_readonly` read a missing `valueDeclaration` as 'no value declaration' and settled a readonly property as mutable (tsrs omits empty fields); a `.unwrap_or(false)` fallback for a missing answer; (2) WORK AHEAD OF A GUARD: classification and decoding ran before the size-budget early-out, a package walk before a cache hit; (3) TESTS THAT DO NOT VARY WHAT THEY CLAIM: a real-checker test varied only `kind` so a parameter tsrs ignores could pass; a process-wide counter in tests; (4) WIRE-CONTRACT COUPLING: `file` vs `files` silently ignored by tsrs (every cold run type-checked the whole program), hard-coded tsrs 0.24 syntax-kind numbers in an allow-list, exact printed type text asserted in tests, `TSRS_READS` a hand copy of tsrs's parameter table; (5) DEGRADE WITHOUT SAYING SO: the project rule is 'always emit a Diagnostic when degrading'; heap-budget and timeout fallbacks, `Result<_, CallError>` paths that turn into structural answers. TASK: sweep crates/semantic/src/** and the hook boundary in crates/core (semantic_hook.rs, types/semantic*, relevance/, pipeline/revision*) for the SAME PATTERNS elsewhere: (a) every `unwrap_or`, `unwrap_or_default`, `.ok()`, `map_or`, `if let Some(..) else` default and `Default::default()` applied to a checker/wire/decoded value where the default is a CLAIM (false, empty, 0, None-as-absent) rather than 'unknown': list file:line, what the default asserts, and when the real value could differ (give the input); (b) every serde `#[serde(default)]`/Option field in the wire structs (`rpc.rs` SymbolWire/TypeInfo/SignatureInfo/etc.) where absence is conflated with 'empty' (tsrs omits empty fields: check `str_nonempty`, `skip_if_empty` style serialisation in tsrs_api/tsrs_checker for each field we decode, in ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/tsrs_api-0.24.0 and tsrs_checker): which of our fields can be absent for TWO different reasons (empty vs not carried), and what do we conclude from absence; (c) guards (budget checks, cache hits, early-outs `past_size_budget`, `heap::step`, `Flights`, memo `recall`) and any decode/classify/allocate/IO work placed BEFORE them in the same function; (d) numeric constants copied from tsrs/TypeScript (syntax kinds, SymbolFlags, CheckFlags, TypeFlags, ObjectFlags in rpc.rs `flag::`): is each pinned to the pinned tsrs version by a test that fails on a bump (the `Cargo.lock` version test pattern from PR #519), and which are not; (e) tests in crates/semantic that assert presence instead of content, vary nothing, or use process-wide state (statics/env/cwd/temp paths): list the weakest 10; (f) every fallback/degrade path (`CallError`, `Fatal`, timeouts, heap budget, `Outcome::unavailable`, structural fallback) and whether a Diagnostic with a stable code is emitted, whether a degraded value is ever cached or compared as authoritative, and how the weekly/bench harnesses could tell the run degraded (they must not match message text: check code and severity). For each hit: file:line, class (a-f), severity (wrong output, wasted work, weak test), a triggering input, a minimal fix. Then 'MODEL AND ARCHITECTURE CHANGES': for example a `Known<T>`/`Evidence<T>` type (Unknown | Settled(T)) that wire decoding returns so an absence cannot be read as a value, a `Degraded` marker/diagnostic channel every fallback must go through, a single `wire` module that owns version-coupled constants with one version-pin test, a test helper `varies::<Param>()`, an architecture test (grep-based) forbidding `unwrap_or(false)` on decoded values; with cost and what each would have prevented among the five. Top 10 hits first. Final message: max 200 words with the path, counts per class and the top 3 changes. Cap 90 tool calls; never ask questions.
